instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Not Why We Drifted
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation away from the real reason the relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I brought our picnic basket. Let's see if you remember how I taught you to lay out a proper lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember our last picnic. You said you needed space. Why?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First correction: don't put the sandwiches in the sun. There's space under that tree; take the blanket over.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Moving won't stop me asking why.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we'll stay. Taste the mustard. You used to say everything was 'nice'; give me a proper criticism this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I found our wedding video. You can finally practise watching faces, like I taught you, instead of just listening to speeches.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd rather discuss why we're living separately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Watch your father's face when he says 'good luck'. Now tell me what he meant.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Exactly this. Pause it. I don't want another speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good observation, wrong conclusion. We'll skip to the dancing. You used to miss all the background action; see if your uncle actually falls into the cake.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Keep the Peace
cards.instruction: Hide a truth because you believe the relationship cannot survive one more conflict.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave that letter under my plate. Remember how I taught you to get through breakfast without an argument? We only just started eating together again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Has your brother cancelled paying us back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're checking the rent. I've covered it. Next lesson: finish your toast before opening things that upset you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then let me open it after breakfast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me clear up first, like I taught you. You finally unpacked yesterday. Please, I can't face another suitcase in the hall.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've spotted the missing savings. Those budget lessons paid off. It's a banking complication; keep our anniversary reservation.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Did you lend your sister money again?

beats.speaker: A

beats.text: I'll ring the bank, then.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let your teacher make this call. You still ask the most explosive question first. Please, I'd like us sharing a table when the money comes back.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Say You Missed Me
cards.instruction: Get someone to admit longing, jealousy, hurt, or attachment before you reveal your own.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now I'm back, give me a straight answer, like I taught you. Was the flat too quiet without me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you tell me whether you missed me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good bargaining. Answer first: when you heard a key, did you hope it was mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Every evening. There, your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a proper answer. Here's your demonstration: I rang our landline just to hear your voice. Could you say hello again?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to price furniture to sell. The sofa's gone, but you're keeping my chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody offered anything. Have you brought its cushion back?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're still dodging the valuation. If someone offered twenty pounds, would you keep it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I like pretending you're about to sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better. I sleep with the cushion. You can stop pretending if you take that price sticker off.

cards.title: We Needed the Break
cards.instruction: Frame a rupture, absence, or failed connection as a healthy decision that ultimately helped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Coffee Sunday? That year apart finally taught you the independence I kept trying to teach you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You used to insist we spend every Saturday together.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Beginner's practice. Eventually the pupil has to stop turning up just because I said so.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've booked pottery this Sunday too.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to keep a plan I didn't make. Coffee Monday, then. I can wait a day for my star pupil.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lunch with just me. That disastrous reunion finally taught you what I meant about taking turns.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We shouted over each other until everyone left.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you got a whole sentence out once the audience had gone. Progress. You always used to play to the crowd.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The waiter just asked if we're expecting twelve more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell him no, just us. Then tell me the rest of that story without winning the room first. I'm giving you all of my turn.

cards.title: I Know How to Fix Us
cards.instruction: Perform confidence about repairing the relationship while improvising every step.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We can fix last night's shouting. I taught you how to discuss things calmly: tea first, then one honest sentence each.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want tea. I want you to listen without interrupting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to state a need. Listening stage: I'll write down anything I want to interrupt with.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll be writing instead of listening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent correction. You're ready to supervise. Take the pen; if I interrupt, write it down and we'll begin with that.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're on stage two of reconciliation. Choose a biscuit. You always did learn better with something to chew.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What was stage one?

beats.speaker: A
